_comment: Generated by client/src/bin/write-fixtures.rs from the doctor's RULES table -- the one shared definition of PUBLISHING.md 3.1.6. Do not edit by hand.
Verified from the registry side by registry/src/rules.test.ts; CI regenerates and fails on any diff, so the two languages cannot drift apart.
what/why/fix are the exact strings a finding renders; id is the contract both sides compile against.

rules.why: VayuWeb blocks inline styles: an attribute selector plus a url() reads your page one character at a time, and a blocked page renders half-dressed.
rules.fix: move the styles into a .css file in your site folder and reference it with <link rel="stylesheet">.

rules.why: VayuWeb blocks inline scripts: they are the main way an injected page steals keystrokes, so a blocked one means your page silently does nothing.
rules.fix: move the code into a .js file in your site folder and load it with <script src="app.js">.

rules.what: a subresource loaded from another server
rules.why: Remote images, scripts and styles do not load on VayuWeb. Every request to another server tells that server who is reading your page.
rules.fix: save the file into your site folder and reference it relatively.

rules.why: This works, but the reader is shown that the link goes outside VayuWeb before following it. That is intended.
rules.fix: nothing needed, unless the target has a copy inside your site folder.

rules.why: data: images are blocked along with other inline content, because their bytes cannot be checked against an address the way real files can.
rules.fix: save the image as a file in your site folder and reference it relatively.

rules.why: <base> rewrites where every relative link on the page points, which is exactly what a tampered page would want. VayuWeb refuses pages that carry one.
rules.fix: remove it and write links the way they should resolve.

rules.why: A frame can host content from anywhere while showing your page's name, so VayuWeb does not render frames at all.
rules.fix: link to the content directly instead of framing it.

rules.what: a form posting to another server
rules.why: Submitting the form sends your reader's input to another server without VayuWeb being able to say so, and static sites have no server to receive it.
rules.fix: point the action at a same-site handler, or replace the form with a mailto: link.

rules.why: dns-prefetch, preconnect, prefetch, preload, prerender and modulepreload all contact another server on the speculation that a reader will click. On VayuWeb they do nothing except leak who is reading.
rules.fix: remove the tag; the resource loads when it is used.

rules.why: The referrer policy is part of the browser-security profile VayuWeb sets for the whole reader session; a page cannot change it.
rules.fix: remove the tag.

rules.why: Auto-redirecting a reader to another address is indistinguishable from open-redirect abuse, so VayuWeb does not honour it.
rules.fix: link to the destination instead, or serve the destination's content directly.

rules.why: WebAssembly runs only when your manifest declares csp.wasm: true, and the reader is told that your site uses it. Undeclared, it is blocked and your app will not start.
rules.fix: add "csp": { "wasm": true } to .vayu/manifest.json, or ship JavaScript instead.

rules.why: A service worker keeps running after the reader leaves, which VayuWeb promises never to allow. Registration is blocked, so code depending on one misbehaves.
rules.fix: remove the registration; cache nothing beyond the reader's visit.

rules.why: A visitor opening your site's root address has no page to land on.
rules.fix: add the index document, or declare "index" in .vayu/manifest.json pointing at your landing page.

rules.what: the whole site is over the hard size ceiling
rules.why: VayuWeb resolvers refuse to serve a site beyond 2 GiB outright, so publishing one means shipping something nobody can open.
rules.fix: split the site into smaller ones, or move large downloads to links outside it.

rules.what: the whole site is over the confirm threshold
rules.why: Sites this large are slow to pin, slow to verify and slow for readers on modest machines; VayuWeb asks you to choose that deliberately.
rules.fix: continue if you meant it -- publishing will ask for confirmation.

rules.what: the whole site is getting large
rules.why: A big tree takes longer to verify on every reader's machine, every time.
rules.fix: nothing required; consider trimming assets you no longer serve.

rules.what: very many files in one directory
rules.why: Tens of thousands of entries in one folder slow every listing and lookup for every reader.
rules.fix: consider nesting folders instead of one flat directory.

rules.what: a single file is over the hard size ceiling
rules.why: Files beyond 256 MiB cannot be fetched within VayuWeb's resource limits, so readers would get an error where the file should be.
rules.fix: compress it, split it, or link to somewhere outside VayuWeb.

rules.what: a single file is quite large
rules.why: One big file makes the whole tree slower to pin and verify.
rules.fix: nothing required; consider compressing it.

rules.why: The manifest tells VayuWeb where your landing page is and what your site needs; one that cannot be read means the checker cannot vouch for anything else.
rules.fix: fix the JSON in .vayu/manifest.json -- it must be a single JSON object.
